description: The molecular biology a computer scientist needs to work with biological data: cells and biomolecules, DNA structure and replication, transcription and translation, genes, genomes and mutation, protein structure and function, the laboratory techniques that generate sequence and expression data, and the databases that store it. Assumes no prior biology and is taught through interactive simulations of molecules and processes and small programs that manipulate real sequences in the browser, at the depth of a first-year molecular biology course for quantitative students.
modelledOn: Alberts et al., Essential Cell Biology
Watson et al., Molecular Biology of the Gene
Lodish et al., Molecular Cell Biology
outcomes: Describe the structure of cells and the main classes of biomolecules and explain how their chemistry determines their function.
Explain DNA structure, replication and repair and represent sequences and their operations as strings and algorithms.
Trace the flow of information from gene to protein through transcription, RNA processing and translation, and implement it in code.
Classify mutations and genomic variation and predict their effects, using sickle cell disease and drug-resistant malaria as worked examples.
Relate protein structure to function and describe how enzymes, receptors and antibodies work.
Explain how sequencing, PCR, microarrays and other laboratory techniques produce data and retrieve and interpret records from biological databases.

units.title: Cells and biomolecules
topics: Why computing needs biology: genomics, drug discovery, epidemiology and precision medicine
Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells; organelles; membranes and transport; viruses as a special case
Chemistry of life: water, bonds, pH; carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids and proteins
Energy and metabolism in outline: enzymes, ATP, respiration and photosynthesis
The cell cycle, mitosis and meiosis; how traits are inherited

units.title: DNA structure and replication
topics: Nucleotides, the double helix, base pairing, antiparallel strands and 5' to 3' direction
Chromosomes, chromatin, histones and packaging; genome sizes across organisms
Semi-conservative replication: helicase, polymerases, primers, leading and lagging strands, Okazaki fragments
Replication errors, proofreading and DNA repair pathways
DNA as data: alphabets, reverse complements, GC content and k-mers written as small programs

units.title: Transcription and translation
topics: The central dogma and its exceptions: reverse transcription in HIV, RNA viruses
Transcription: promoters, RNA polymerase, transcription factors, termination
RNA processing in eukaryotes: capping, polyadenylation, splicing and alternative splicing
The genetic code: codons, reading frames, start and stop codons, codon usage; translating sequences in code
Translation: ribosomes, tRNA, initiation, elongation, termination; post-translational modification
Gene regulation: operons, enhancers, epigenetics and non-coding RNAs in outline

units.title: Genes, genomes and mutation
topics: Gene structure: exons, introns, untranslated regions, regulatory regions; genome organisation and repeats
Types of mutation: substitutions, insertions, deletions, frameshifts, copy number and structural variants
Sickle cell disease: the single substitution in the beta-globin gene, inheritance patterns and its prevalence in West Africa
Malaria and human genetics: the sickle cell trait, G6PD deficiency and balancing selection
Pathogen genomes: Plasmodium falciparum, drug-resistance mutations and genomic surveillance
Population genetics in brief: alleles, Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, African genetic diversity

units.title: Proteins and their functions
topics: Amino acids and their properties; peptide bonds
Levels of structure: primary, secondary, tertiary and quaternary; folding and misfolding
Haemoglobin and how one amino acid change causes sickling
Enzymes and kinetics in outline; inhibitors and drug targets such as antimalarials
Antibodies, receptors and signalling; vaccines and the immune response
Predicting and visualising protein structure; the impact of structure prediction models

units.title: Laboratory techniques that produce data
topics: Extraction, gel electrophoresis, restriction enzymes and cloning
PCR and quantitative PCR; rapid diagnostic tests for malaria and their limits
Sanger sequencing and next-generation sequencing: reads, quality scores, FASTQ files, coverage; long-read and portable sequencing
Measuring expression: microarrays and RNA-seq; mass spectrometry for proteins
Genome editing with CRISPR-Cas9 and its ethical questions
Sources of error and noise in experimental data; replicates and controls

units.title: Biological databases
topics: Sequence formats: FASTA, GenBank and FASTQ; parsing them with code
Primary databases: GenBank, ENA and DDBJ; UniProt for proteins and the Protein Data Bank for structures
Genome browsers, Ensembl and variant databases such as dbSNP and ClinVar
Searching with BLAST and interpreting a result; ontologies such as the Gene Ontology
Data sharing, consent and benefit-sharing in African genomics research; capstone: annotate a malaria parasite gene from database records

schedule.title: Cells and the chemistry of life
schedule.exercise: Draw and label a prokaryotic and a eukaryotic cell side by side, and write two sentences on why the differences matter for drug design.

tasks.title: Classify twelve cell structures by cell type and function in a guided scenario, and explain one misclassification the case exposes
Match five biomolecules to their roles in a malaria case study, using evidence on what each one does in the parasite and the patient
Choose which of three computing projects in drug discovery, epidemiology and precision medicine best fits a given clinic need, with reasons scored by rubric

schedule.title: Metabolism and inheritance
schedule.exercise: Work three Punnett square problems for a recessive trait and write the expected ratios and what a carrier parent means.

tasks.title: Simulate the inheritance of one recessive trait across 1000 offspring from two carrier parents and compare the counts with the expected 3 to 1 ratio
Step through glycolysis and respiration in a visualiser, track ATP made at each stage, and total the energy yield per glucose molecule
Simulate mitosis and meiosis on a small genome, track chromosome number and allele mixing, and show how meiosis produces variation

schedule.title: DNA structure and replication
schedule.exercise: Explain in a paragraph why replication is semi-conservative and why the lagging strand needs Okazaki fragments.

tasks.title: Write a function that returns the complementary strand and reads 5 prime to 3 prime direction for five short DNA sequences
Compare genome sizes of six organisms against their chromosome numbers and gene counts, and discuss why size does not track complexity
Step through replication of a DNA segment, labelling the leading strand, lagging strand and Okazaki fragments at each fork step

schedule.title: Repair and DNA as data
schedule.exercise: Describe three DNA repair pathways and the type of damage each fixes, then link each to a disease that follows from its failure.

tasks.title: Compute the GC content and reverse complement of five DNA sequences with a short program and check one by hand
Count all k-mers of length 3 in a DNA sequence of 500 bases and plot the most frequent ones
Simulate replication with a given error rate and proofreading success, count mutations over many generations, and compare with the expected value

schedule.title: Transcription and RNA processing
schedule.exercise: Draw the flow from gene to mature mRNA, marking promoter, exons, introns, cap and tail, and say where each step can go wrong.

tasks.title: Step through transcription of a gene with a promoter and terminator and record the RNA sequence produced
Splice a pre-mRNA with three exons, then use alternative splicing to create two different mature mRNAs and compare their lengths
Explain from a case on HIV and an RNA virus why reverse transcription is a target for drugs, and rank three drug ideas by evidence

schedule.title: The genetic code and translation
schedule.exercise: Write the protein produced by a short mRNA by hand using the codon table, and show the effect of a one-base insertion.

tasks.title: Translate a DNA sequence into a protein in all three forward reading frames using a codon table and find the longest open reading frame
Step through ribosome translation of an mRNA, tracking tRNA binding, peptide growth and termination at the stop codon
Analyse a case on an operon with a regulator mutation and decide, from the expression data, whether the gene is always on, always off or normal

schedule.title: Genes, mutation and sickle cell disease
schedule.exercise: Write a short explanation of how a single base change in the beta-globin gene leads to sickle cell disease and how it is inherited.

tasks.title: Classify ten mutations in a gene as substitution, insertion or deletion and as silent, missense, nonsense or frameshift by translating each
Compare the normal and sickle beta-globin sequences, find the substitution, and compute the expected inheritance ratios for carrier parents
Annotate the exons, introns and regulatory regions of a sample gene model, and judge which of three variants is most likely harmful

schedule.title: Malaria, pathogen genomes and populations
schedule.exercise: Explain why the sickle cell trait persists in malaria regions, using the idea of balancing selection with a simple numeric example.

tasks.title: Compute genotype frequencies under Hardy-Weinberg for an allele frequency of 0.1 and compare them with a sample of observed counts
Simulate selection on the sickle allele with and without malaria over 100 generations and plot the allele frequency in each case
Interpret genomic surveillance data on drug-resistance mutations in Plasmodium falciparum and recommend a change in treatment policy from the evidence

schedule.title: Amino acids and protein structure
schedule.exercise: Sort the twenty amino acids by property in a table, and predict which kinds of substitution would most disturb a protein.

tasks.title: Compute the length and net charge of three short peptides from their sequences using an amino acid property table
Fold a short peptide in a simple lattice model, step by step, and compare the energy of folded and unfolded forms
Explain the haemoglobin sickling case from structure data, identifying which interactions the substitution creates and how they cause fibres

schedule.title: Enzymes, immunity and structure prediction
schedule.exercise: Write a short note on how an antimalarial drug can inhibit an enzyme, with the type of inhibition and the effect on reaction rate.

tasks.title: Compute reaction rates from the Michaelis-Menten equation for six substrate levels and plot the curve with its maximum rate
Add a competitive inhibitor to the enzyme model and show how the apparent Km changes while the maximum rate stays the same
Judge three structure predictions of a drug target using confidence scores, and decide which regions you would trust for drug design

schedule.title: Laboratory methods and sequencing data
schedule.exercise: Plan a PCR and gel experiment to detect a pathogen gene in a blood sample, listing controls and what each band pattern would mean.

tasks.title: Digest a DNA sequence with two restriction enzymes in code, list the fragment sizes, and draw the expected gel pattern
Model PCR amplification over 30 cycles with a given efficiency and find the cycle at which the signal crosses the detection threshold
Parse a small FASTQ file, convert quality scores, trim low-quality ends and report the coverage of a short reference

schedule.title: Expression, editing and noise
schedule.exercise: Write a short ethics note on a proposed CRISPR therapy for sickle cell disease, covering benefit, risk, access and consent.

tasks.title: Compare measurements from three replicates and one control, compute mean and spread, and decide whether a difference is larger than the noise
Compute fold change from an RNA-seq count table for ten genes, normalise by library size, and list those changed more than twofold
Decide whether to approve a genome-editing trial in a case with scientific, consent and equity issues, scored against a rubric

schedule.title: Biological data and databases
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: annotate one malaria parasite gene using database records, giving its location, product, function, variants and sources.

tasks.title: Parse a FASTA file of five sequences, report each length and base composition, and write the sequences back out in a valid format
Interpret a BLAST result for a mystery sequence from a case, reading e-values and identity to decide what the sequence most likely is
Annotate a malaria parasite gene from database records and design a data-sharing and consent plan for a related African study, scored against a rubric
